_note: Weather, wind, temperature, visibility and avalanche numbers. Times are mountain time. Wind speeds are m/s, temperatures °C, visibility metres.
_conditions: Each kind of weather. cloud: sky cover 0..1. snow: snowfall 0..1 (1 is about 3 cm an hour). visibility_m: how far you see in it. wind: multiplier on the day's wind. temp: °C offset. fade_min: how fast it arrives (a whiteout can close in within minutes). hours: how long a spell lasts, min and max.
_transitions: Chance of each next spell after the current one. Afternoon (afternoon_hours) adds afternoon_storm_bonus to the chance of snow and storm, as summer clouds build over the Karakoram after midday.
_temperature: Air temperature at reference_altitude swings from day_low_c before dawn to day_high_c in the afternoon, and drops lapse_c_per_km with height, so it is about -25 °C on the summit at night. Clear nights are colder, cloud keeps the warmth in.
_wind: Calm low down, rising toward the jet stream near the summit. Ridges and high shoulders catch it all; hollows and couloirs are sheltered. Gusts come every few seconds of real time. Direction drifts around the prevailing westerly.
_wind_on_climber: Wind above push_from_m_s pushes you downwind (push_m_s per m/s, real time, more when standing on steep ground) and headwind slows you. Gusts over knockdown_m_s can throw you off balance on steep unroped ground. On the rope the push is a third.
_visibility: Inside the cloud band (cloud_base_m to cloud_top_m, only when cloud cover is over 0.5) visibility drops to in_cloud_visibility_m. Clouds and fog drift through, so visibility flickers by up to flicker of itself over a few minutes. Strong wind lifts spindrift off ridges.
_snowpack: Snow builds up during snowfall (snow 1 = snow_cm_per_hour) and settles away at settle_cm_per_hour, faster when warm. Wind over load_from_m_s drifts it into slabs on lee slopes.
_avalanche: Danger 0..1 from fresh snow (full at danger_fresh_cm), wind slab and afternoon warming. Natural slides run on snow slopes between slab_min_deg and slab_max_deg somewhere above you; crossing such a slope can set one off yourself. Being caught knocks you into a tumble; ending up buried hurts.
_serac: The hanging serac above the Bottleneck. Ice breaks off it now and then, most in the warmth of the day; the blocks come down the couloir. serac_grid is its place on the heightmap.
_forecast: In a camp you hear the radio forecast for the next forecast_hours; it gets the timing wrong by up to forecast_error_hours.
